newsitem.title: USA: Life Partners says court denies re-hearing.
newsitem.headline: Life Partners says court denies re-hearing.

text.p: Privately held Life Partners Inc said on Monday that the U.S. Court of Appeals declined the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's bid to re-hear a case against the company.

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has contended that the viatical settlement company should be regulated as a securities firm, but the courts have not shared that view, a spokesman for Life Partners said.
As a viatical settlement company, Life Partners buys life insurance policies from the terminally ill at a discount and then collects the policy's full value when the insured dies.
Life Partners said the Court of Appeals had thrown out an earlier case on July 5, 1996, that the SEC had brought against the company.
The company said it is unlikely that the SEC would take the case to the U.S. Supreme Court, since the SEC's petition to re-hear it was rejected by the appeals panel.
A company spokesman said Life Partners, which has purchased about $300 million of insurance policies, is regulated by state insurance departments.
